memoryTip: Mutilate = maim: seriously harm or disfigure something.
correctPassage: Vandals mutilated the statue beyond easy repair.
wrongPassages: Restorers hoped to mutilate the painting by cleaning dust from the frame only.
The monitor will mutilate escalations by looping them into a channel nobody reads.
To mutilate the dispute, both sides published a joint statement of full agreement.

memoryTip: In-genuous: genuine innocence — not scheming (not ingenious!).
correctPassage: Her ingenuous questions revealed how little the brochure had explained.
wrongPassages: His ingenuous scheme used three shell companies and a forged audit trail.
The spy’s ingenuous cover story was rehearsed for months and left no loose ends.
An ingenuous negotiator outmaneuvered every rival with careful misdirection.

memoryTip: In-genius: clever invention (don’t confuse with ingenuous!).
correctPassage: An ingenious use of recycled materials kept construction costs low.
wrongPassages: Critics called the plan ingenious because it copied last year’s memo word for word.
An ingenious worksheet asked only for the student’s name written once.
He packed a spare ingenious in the trunk next to the tire and jumper cables.

definition: not showing care for the consequences of an action
memoryTip: Im-prudent: not prudent — careless about consequences.
correctPassage: Borrowing against future revenue was widely seen as imprudent.
wrongPassages: The plan looked imprudent on paper: every risk already removed and every owner named.
Her imprudent budget set aside emergency reserves and deferred nonessential spending.
Judges called the ruling imprudent because it carefully weighed both sides and cited law.

definition: be a sign or warning of (a future event)
memoryTip: Pre-sage: a sign before the event — an omen.
correctPassage: Darkening skies seemed to presage a severe storm.
wrongPassages: Please presage the chairs into neat rows for the next panel.
They packed a spare presage in the trunk next to the tire and jumper cables.
After lunch the staff agreed to presage the budget by printing extra copies.
